advisory.unencrypted_data_channel: The data channel uses no cipher: everything sent through the tunnel can be read and changed on the way. Use this only if the provider gives no other option.
advisory.unencrypted_data_channel_allowed: The profile allows an unencrypted data channel ("none" in Cipher). This connection negotiated a cipher and is encrypted; remove "none" from the Cipher field so that it stays that way.
advisory.weak_cipher: The cipher is outdated. Prefer AES-256-GCM or CHACHA20-POLY1305 if the server supports them.
advisory.weak_digest: The authentication digest is weak. Prefer SHA256 or an AEAD cipher.
advisory.compression_enabled: Compression is enabled. It is deprecated and can leak data (VORACLE).
advisory.tls_auth_instead_of_crypt: tls-auth is used; tls-crypt also hides the handshake.
advisory.server_usage_check_disabled: The check that the server certificate is issued for a server is off.
advisory.fragment_in_use: fragment is set: a legacy workaround for MTU problems that slows the tunnel.
advisory.no_dco: This host's kernel has no data channel offload; expect lower throughput.

code.runs_code: runs programs or scripts, which TunnelDeck-VPN does not allow.

code.managed_by_field: is set through a profile field.
code.deprecated_ignored: is deprecated and ignored by OpenVPN.
code.windows_only_ignored: only applies to OpenVPN clients on Windows and is left out.
code.invalid_directive: is not a valid OpenVPN directive.
code.inline_block: inline blocks are only allowed for keys and certificates.
code.invalid_value: has a value TunnelDeck-VPN cannot use.
code.file_reference: refers to the file {{file}}, which is not part of the profile. Embed its content in the .ovpn file, or paste it into the highlighted field.
code.additional_remote: is an additional server; only the first one is used.
code.unsupported_device: sets a device type TunnelDeck-VPN does not support.
code.inline_block_unsupported: is an inline block TunnelDeck-VPN does not support.
code.cipher_mapped: was converted to the current cipher setting.
code.compression_receive_only: compression is accepted from the server but not used for sending.
code.compression_kept: compression stays on because the server requires it.
code.ns_cert_type_mapped: was replaced by the server certificate check.
code.server_cert_usage_added: The server certificate check was switched on.
code.static_key_unsupported: uses static-key mode, which is insecure and deprecated; use certificates or username and password instead.
code.setenv_ignored: sets a variable that only scripts and VPN apps use; it is not needed.
code.script_security_dropped: only allows scripts; TunnelDeck-VPN runs none, so it is not needed.
code.verb_replaced: was replaced by the log level of TunnelDeck-VPN.
code.credentials_expected: The file contains no client certificate and no username and password. Sign-in with username and password is selected: enter the access data from your provider.
code.credentials_from_partial_block: Username and password were taken from a credentials block that is only partly commented out.
code.unknown_directive: is not a known OpenVPN option.
code.dns_ignored: is not applied; the host's DNS settings stay unchanged.
code.listen_port_ignored: is not needed; TunnelDeck-VPN picks a free port.
code.save_config_ignored: only matters to wg-quick and is not needed.
code.ipv6_ignored: has IPv6 entries, which are left out; only IPv4 is used.
code.additional_address: names a further IPv4 address; only the first one is used.
code.additional_peer: is a further peer; only the first peer is used.
code.keepalive_default: is not set; 25 seconds are used so that the tunnel stays reachable from the server.
code.unknown_key: is not a known WireGuard setting.

hint.tun-device: Pass the TUN device into the container (devices: /dev/net/tun).
hint.iptables: Install iptables in the image and make sure the host kernel provides the iptables filter table.
hint.net-admin: Grant the container the NET_ADMIN capability (cap_add: NET_ADMIN).
hint.ip-forward: Enable IPv4 forwarding on the host (sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward=1, persisted in /etc/sysctl.conf); Docker hosts normally have it on. Without it, rules to other devices and outbound rules forward nothing.
hint.lan-subnets: Run the container with network_mode: host on a host that has an IPv4 address on its LAN interface.
hint.rule-counters: Load the comment match on the host (modprobe xt_comment), or use the nft backend (TUNNELDECK_IPTABLES=nft), then restart the container. The firewall works without it; only the hit counters are off.
hint.syn-flood-protection: Load the hashlimit match on the host (modprobe xt_hashlimit; the limit match, xt_limit, allows a global limit), then restart the container. Some NAS kernels do not ship these modules; the firewall works without them.
hint.ping-limit: Load the hashlimit match on the host (modprobe xt_hashlimit; the limit match, xt_limit, allows a global limit), then restart the container. Some NAS kernels do not ship these modules; the firewall works without them.
hint.mss-clamp: Load the TCPMSS target on the host (modprobe xt_TCPMSS), then restart the container. Some NAS kernels do not ship it; the firewall works without it, but large transfers through the tunnel may stall.
hint.reject-target: Load the REJECT target on the host (modprobe ipt_REJECT), then restart the container. Some NAS kernels do not ship it; the firewall works without it, but reject rules drop silently.
hint.reply-routing: Load the connmark module and the mangle table on the host (modprobe xt_connmark iptable_mangle), then restart the container. Port forwards work without them, but a device that receives a port forward and uses this device as its gateway sends all its traffic through the tunnel while it is up.

detail.iptablesForced: Uses {{binary}}: the {{backend}} backend is set by configuration.
detail.iptablesOnlyNft: Uses {{binary}}: only the nf_tables backend works.
detail.iptablesOnlyLegacy: Uses {{binary}}: only the legacy backend works.
detail.iptablesMixed: Uses {{binary}}: both backends hold host rules (nf_tables {{nftRules}}, legacy {{legacyRules}}), {{backend}} has more. The other backend's rules still apply.
detail.iptablesRulesLegacy: Uses {{binary}}: only the legacy backend holds host rules ({{legacyRules}}).
detail.iptablesRulesNft: Uses {{binary}}: only the nf_tables backend holds host rules ({{nftRules}}).
detail.iptablesNoRules: Uses {{binary}}: neither backend holds host rules, so nf_tables is preferred.
detail.netAdminWorks: A test chain was created and deleted.
detail.netAdminFailed: Creating or deleting a test chain failed: {{error}}
detail.lanNone: No IPv4 address on a LAN interface.
detail.lanFailed: The LAN subnets cannot be detected: {{error}}
detail.extensionsUnverified: The iptables extensions cannot be checked: {{error}}
detail.countersOn: The iptables comment match is available; hit counters are on.
detail.countersOff: The iptables comment match ({{module}}) is unavailable, so hit counters are off.
detail.synFloodFull: Uses the hashlimit match: one rate per sender.
detail.synFloodGlobal: The hashlimit match ({{module}}) is unavailable, so the protection falls back to the {{fallback}} match: one global rate for all senders instead of one per sender.
detail.synFloodNone: Neither the hashlimit match ({{module}}) nor the limit match ({{fallbackModule}}) is available, so SYN flood protection is left out of the firewall.
detail.pingNone: Neither the hashlimit match ({{module}}) nor the limit match ({{fallbackModule}}) is available, so the ping limit is left out of the firewall.
detail.mssClampOff: The TCPMSS target ({{module}}) is unavailable, so MSS clamping is left out of the firewall.
detail.rejectMissing: The REJECT target ({{module}}) is unavailable, so reject rules drop instead and send no answer.
detail.replyRoutingConnmark: Replies of port forwards follow a connection mark (CONNMARK in the mangle table).
detail.replyRoutingFallback: The CONNMARK target ({{module}}) or the mangle table ({{table}}) is unavailable, so replies of port forwards are routed by the target's address: everything this device routes for a port-forward target goes through the tunnel while it is up.

publicIpLookup.title: Public IP detection
publicIpLookup.description: After every connect, TunnelDeck-VPN asks a service through the tunnel which public IPv4 address the internet sees. The dashboard and the remote access address show it unless the profile names a public address, which always takes precedence.
publicIpLookup.urlHint: An http or https address that answers with the IPv4 address as plain text.
publicIpLookup.privacy: The service sees the public IP address of the tunnel and the name TunnelDeck-VPN as user agent; nothing else is sent. The host resolves the service name with its usual DNS server, not through the tunnel.
